correctness.rationale: For all integers \(m\ge1\), degree constraints restrict each simplex to at most one outgoing page arrow, one incoming page arrow and the common arrow. Exactly the same-index triple is a directed cycle. Every off-diagonal page pair is the unique free edge of its corresponding 2-simplex; removing all \(m(m-1)\) distinct free-face pairs leaves m triangles as unfilled graph cycles wedged at the common edge-vertex. The collapse is permutation-equivariant because every pair is carried to another pair with no inverted simplex and simultaneous deformations agree on the retained intersections. Therefore every subgroup H has fixed homotopy type a wedge of \(f_H\) circles and quotient type a wedge of \(o_H\) circles; the first integral homology is the page-permutation lattice. Standalone exact enumeration for m=1..7 and full two-generator subgroup tests of \(S_4\) reproduce this combinatorics.

value.rationale: The natural \(m\)-page shared-arrow directed book contains an arbitrary number of overlapping directed cycles and is directly motivated by a published open direction for directed forest complexes with cycles. The result computes an explicit symmetry-compatible simple-homotopy reduction for every \(m\), identifies the integral fundamental-group generator action and computes all subgroup fixed and orbit homotopy types (different functions \(f_H\) versus \(o_H\)), information not implied by the nonequivariant Betti numbers and not merely a finite table. The face-pair matching is a reusable constructive tool in orientation-sensitive multipath topology.
